name: Narratology: Foundations, Domains, Frontiers
description: The course will familiarise students with the history of narratology in Russian formalism, structural linguistics and anthropology, and then its entry into literary studies, discourse and stylistics. The course will impart an application-based understanding of advanced narratological concepts and the debates among the prominent narratological schools since the 1970s. The spread of narrative theory beyond literary research to other areas such as comic books and video games, as well as its relevance to other disciplinary inquires in sociology, legal studies, political theory, postcolonial theory and psychology will be discussed. The course will consider the philosophical questions of narrative and temporality, anti-narrative, subjectivity, language, action, personhood, framing, closure and evolutionary theory, as well as studies of gender, race, history, ideology, culture, and cognition.
